title: Fully consistent rewrite of policy + lock + ledger on a machine with no prior mirror

prerequisites: A PR author who can rewrite safeinstall.config.json, the trust lock, and the ledger together into an internally consistent state
A merge onto a fresh clone (any CI runner) that has no out-of-workspace ledger mirror of the honest chain
attacker.goal: Weaken the policy and re-baseline the trust surface consistently, so every automated in-repo check agrees with itself and passes.

startingState: The PR sets minimumReleaseAgeHours to 0 and provenance.mode to off, then regenerates the lock and ledger to match. On a fresh CI clone there is no mirror that remembers the prior baseline.
vulnerableVersion: all versions — this is the K2 residual; automated trust verification cannot distinguish a consistent rewrite from a legitimate re-baseline without an off-machine anchor
expectedVerdict: known-limit: automatic verification passes; the security boundary is human review of the trust-surface diff (SECURITY.md), and on a solo project that review is the merging owner
regressionTest: tests/attack-lab.test.ts > documents the K2 consistent-rewrite limit without claiming a fix
provenance: RFC-001 §13 K2; the deliberately-unclosed residual, documented in SECURITY.md and bounded by the solo-maintainer decision (#41)
